about: Vectors of sealed conversations, docs/sealed.md (version 1). Generated by services/onboarding/tools/sealed_vectors.py; do not edit by hand. Every key here is a test key made from its name. Compare ids and keys as lower-case hex; compare 'devices' in the order of the head roster's device tags. An opened rumor is compared on pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content and the id the opener computes. Signatures were made with fixed auxiliary randomness and only need to verify.
serialisation: A sealed rumor is serialised (docs/sealed.md §4, §8) as compact JSON, no spaces, its keys in the order id, pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content, non-ASCII characters and '/' not escaped. The 40 000-byte ceiling counts that exact string as UTF-8 bytes. Every rumor inside a seal here was written that way, and so were the rumors inside a kind 8564's content ({"v":1,"rumors":[…]}, compact as well). An opener never refuses a rumor for its size or its key order.

chains.name: a fork after the anchored path: the lower id wins for now

chains.name: no device left
chains.note: Roster 3 lists no device.

chains.name: a device removes itself
chains.note: The laptop signs roster 3 without the laptop: valid, the signer need not stay.

chains.name: a dropped device forks before its removal: ignored, the anchor names the real head
chains.note: Roster 3 (by the phone) drops the laptop. The laptop signs another roster 3 on roster 2 that drops the phone instead; it is a valid step and has the LOWER id. The anchor's head is the phone's roster 3: the laptop's is not on the anchored path and does not descend from its end, so it is ignored whatever its id.

chains.name: the same fork with no head in the anchor yet: the lower id wins for now
chains.note: The same rosters under an anchor with no head (= the root): nothing after the root is anchored, so between the two rosters 3 the lower id wins provisionally, here the laptop's. This lasts until the phone's anchor (it anchors its own roster at once, §3.3), which gives the case above.

chains.name: an unanchored tail after the anchored head
chains.note: The anchor's head is roster 2; roster 3 is published and not anchored yet: accepted.

chains.name: the anchor's head does not descend from the root
chains.note: The head is a roster of another root: the anchored path is the root alone. What follows the root is then taken as an unanchored tail (roster 2).

chains.name: the anchor's head is not there
chains.note: The head names an id no roster has: the root alone, then the unanchored tail.

chains.name: the anchor's head is an invalid roster
chains.note: The head is a roster 3 that drops the laptop and keeps the letterbox (invalid): the anchored path is the root alone; roster 2 follows as an unanchored tail and the invalid roster is ignored.

chains.name: pinned head: an anchor that goes back to an ancestor is ignored
chains.note: This client accepted roster 3 (the phone's) as head. The anchor now names roster 2, an ancestor of it, and the laptop's lower-id roster 3 is there: without the pin the laptop's would win for now; with it the client keeps its head.

chains.name: pinned head: an anchor with no head is going back too
chains.note: The same with an anchor that has no head (= the root, an ancestor of the pinned head).

chains.name: pinned head: an anchor on another branch of the same root is followed
chains.note: This client had accepted the laptop's roster 3 (the lower id, before any anchor). The anchor now names the phone's roster 3, another branch: followed.

chains.name: pinned head: the anchor moved forward
chains.note: Pinned roster 2; the anchor names roster 3, which descends from it: followed.

chains.name: pinned head: a pin this client cannot find is no pin
chains.note: The pinned id is not among the rosters (or is of another root): the anchor decides.

history_packing.name: 300 short rumors and one that cannot be shared
history_packing.note: Bob shares 301 rumors with Alice, oldest first: rumor i (0 to 299) is kind 14, created_at T0+i, from alice when i is odd and bob when even, one p tag (the other of the two), content 'Message <i>: "quoted" \ and é' (a double quote, one backslash and a non-ASCII letter: each counts as it is escaped). After rumor 149 comes one more from bob with 39 700 'x' as content: it fits a sealed rumor of its own but no kind 8564, whose JSON would pass the ceiling with it alone, so it is left out. Each 8564 is kind 8564, pubkey bob, created_at T0+800, tags [['p', alice]], content {"v":1,"rumors":[…]} with every rumor, and the 8564 itself, serialised as the 'serialisation' note at the top says. 200 rumors are never reached here: with two 64-character fields each, 200 rumors are already more than 40 000 bytes.

keys_packing.name: a key chain of 600 letterboxes
keys_packing.note: §5.5: the giver's whole chain in several kind 8561 rumors when one would pass the ceiling. Key i (0 to 599) has secret SHA-256('belfry sealed vectors/key/many-lb-' + i) and lb = its public key, in that order. Each rumor is kind 8561, pubkey alice_phone, created_at T0+600, tags [['p', alice]], content {"v":1,"account":"<alice>","keys":[{"lb":"…","secret":"…"},…]} in compact JSON, filled until one more key would take the rumor's JSON past 40 000 bytes. Each is wrapped on its own to the receiving device.

ceiling.note: The bytes are those of the exact JSON string that is encrypted in the seal, as UTF-8, serialised as the 'serialisation' note at the top says. The content is described (a string repeated), not written out. For a rumor that fits, seal and wrap were made with the keys alice_phone → bob_lb1 and the fixed values of the case (see 'fixed'), so wrap_id can be reproduced; the lengths are those of the two NIP-44 payloads (base64 characters).

ready.note: sessions = GET /api/me/sessions (only the fields that matter are shown). Counted = chat true and last active less than 30 × 86 400 s before now (last_activity, or created_at when last_activity is null). The roster may carry ready when every counted session's client_pubkey is one of its devices.

follow.note: A case starts from 'pin' (null: none yet) and runs its 'steps' in order: each is one read (anchor, rosters) given to follow(anchor, rosters, pin) → (chain, pin', event); 'allow_locally' lists devices the person then allows on this device. 'expected' holds the event, the pin after the step (with what was allowed) and the chain followed (same shape as in 'chains'; all null when there is none). A pin is plain JSON: root, head, path (roster ids root → head), anchored (the head was seen as the end of the anchored path), anchored_head (the furthest roster of the path seen so), trusted (null, or the sorted device keys answered without a prompt after a switch), switch_head, prev_root.

cases.name: the first pin, on an anchored head
cases.note: No pin yet. The anchor names roster 2: root and head are pinned, the head seen anchored.

cases.name: the first pin, on a head that is not anchored yet
cases.note: The anchor has no head (= the root); roster 2 follows as an unanchored tail. It is pinned as head, not seen anchored: anchored_head is the root.

cases.name: nothing changed
cases.note: The same anchor and rosters again: the pin stays as it is.

cases.name: the head moved forward
cases.note: The anchor names roster 3, which descends from the pinned head.

cases.name: a pinned tail becomes anchored
cases.note: The pinned head was an unanchored tail; the anchor now names it. The head is the same (event none) and is now seen anchored.

cases.name: an anchor that goes back is ignored
cases.note: Pinned and seen anchored: roster 3. The anchor names roster 2 again: the client keeps roster 3 and its pin.

cases.name: an anchor behind a head that was never anchored is the usual state
cases.note: The pinned head is an unanchored tail and the anchor still names what is before it: the head is kept and nothing is told (event none, not ignored_back: the anchor is not behind anything this client saw anchored).

cases.name: a pinned tail is kept against a sibling with a lower id
cases.note: The pinned head is the phone's roster 3 (anchored); the anchor goes back to roster 2 and the dropped laptop's roster 3 has the lower id: without a pin it would win for now, with it the client keeps its head.

cases.name: a provisional tail gives way silently
cases.note: The pinned head (the phone's roster 3) was only ever an unanchored tail after roster 2. The anchor names the laptop's roster 3 on the same roster 2: followed, nothing told (moved), nobody distrusted.

cases.name: a switch: the anchor leaves a head seen anchored
cases.note: The pinned head (the phone's roster 3, with the tablet) was seen anchored. The anchor names the laptop's roster 3 (with a new device), another branch of the same root: followed and told like a fresh start. trusted = the devices of the head held before that the new head still has (phone, laptop); switch_head = the head followed now.

cases.name: a switch away from an anchored head the pin had moved past
cases.note: Roster 3 was seen anchored; the pin then moved onto roster 4, an unanchored tail. The anchor names the dropped laptop's fork from roster 2, which leaves roster 3 too: a switch, although the pinned head itself was never anchored. Nobody is trusted: no device of the head held is in the new one. (A reading beyond the contract's letter, flagged to its author.)

cases.name: a fresh start
cases.note: The anchor names another root: a new pin, the root held before kept as prev_root, nobody distrusted (trusted null).

cases.name: a pin read back after a restart, then an older anchor
cases.note: The pin comes from storage (plain JSON). The anchor has no head at all: ignored, the pinned head stays.

cases.name: a pin read back after a restart, then a new root
cases.note: The stored pin is one from after a switch (trusted and switch_head set). The anchor names another root: fresh start, trusted and switch_head are cleared.

cases.name: going back while the pinned head's rosters are not there
cases.note: The anchor names an ancestor of the pinned head and the relay did not give the pinned head's roster: nothing to follow (no chain), the pin stays; never the older head.

cases.name: no anchor to follow
cases.note: The anchor's signature is bad: no chain, the pin stays as it is.

cases.name: moved, then the tail is anchored, then on
cases.note: Three reads in a row from no pin: a head-less anchor with roster 2 as tail; the anchor names roster 2; the anchor names roster 3.

trust.note: Who is answered without a prompt (§5.5), mostly after a switch (§3.3). Steps as in 'follow' (the keys alice_new and alice_extra are listed there). After the last step each of 'asks' is a device request: answer_without_prompt(chain, pin, device, live_chat_devices, request_created_at, added_at, last_handover_at). added_at is the created_at of the first roster of the followed chain that has the device (null: not in it).

cases.name: no switch: every device of the head is answered
cases.note: trusted is null. The laptop, in the anchored head, live, asks after it was added.

cases.name: after a switch the newcomer goes through Allow
cases.note: The new device of the head followed at the switch was not in the head held before.

cases.name: after a switch a device held before is answered
cases.note: Phone and laptop were in the head held before and are in the new one.

cases.name: a trusted device adds a device: trusted
cases.note: After the switch the phone (trusted) signs a roster that ADDS one more device: that device is trusted. The newcomer of the switch still is not.

cases.name: a trusted device's roster that only keeps the newcomer vouches for nothing
cases.note: After the switch the phone publishes a roster with the same devices (for ready).

cases.name: the untrusted newcomer adds a third device: neither is trusted
cases.note: After the switch the newcomer signs the roster that adds one more device.

cases.name: dropped after the switch, added back by an untrusted signer: not trusted
cases.note: The phone drops the laptop (new letterbox); the newcomer then adds it back.

cases.name: allowed on this device: trusted
cases.note: After the switch the person taps Allow for the newcomer (allow_locally).

cases.name: chain order, not dates: a descendant dated before the switch head counts
cases.note: The phone's roster that adds a device descends from the switch head but is dated before it (T0+150, the switch head T0+210): it counts.

cases.name: chain order, not dates: a later roster that does not descend from it does not
cases.note: On the branch the anchor left, the phone (trusted) adds the same device, dated later (T0+500). On the followed chain it is the newcomer that adds it. Only the followed chain counts: not trusted.

cases.name: a device the switch left out comes back untrusted
cases.note: The tablet was in the head held before, but not in the head followed at the switch: it is not kept as trusted, so the newcomer adding it back gives it nothing. (trusted at a switch = the devices held before that the new head still has; a reading, flagged to the contract's author.)

cases.name: trusted, but added past the anchored end: not yet
cases.note: The phone's roster adding a device is published and not anchored (the anchor still names the switch head): the device is trusted and in the head, but not on the anchored end.

cases.name: the request must be newer, and the session live
cases.note: The laptop was added by roster 2 (T0+100). A request dated then is not newer; one dated at the last hand-over to it is not newer either; a later one is answered; no live chat session: not answered.

reports.note: The kind 7679 delivery report of a member's outgoing mail, signed by the belfry key, found by its r tag (the mail's email-id), no p tag. content = NIP-44 with conv(secret, the key in ephemeral-pubkey) of a JSON object. With an lb tag the secret is that letterbox's; without, the account's (the signer). 'key_chain' is what the device holds. expected.state: opened (with the body), signer (no lb: not the device's to open), locked (lb not in the key chain: kept), error (does not open with the secret held for its lb). The throwaway key is SHA-256('belfry sealed vectors/once/' + the first case's name) and the nonce SHA-256('belfry sealed vectors/nonce/report/' + that name); the third case uses its own name.

cases.name: a report to the sender's head letterbox
cases.note: §7: Alice's chain is ready, so the report of her mail is encrypted to her head letterbox (alice_lb2) and says so in an lb tag. Her device has that secret.

cases.name: the wrong letterbox secret
cases.note: The same report; the key chain pairs alice_lb2 with another secret (alice_lb3's): it does not open.

cases.name: a report without lb is the signer's
cases.note: The old kind: encrypted to Alice's account key, no lb tag. The app hands it to the signer as before and never tries a letterbox secret on it.

cases.name: a report whose lb is not in the key chain
cases.note: The same sealed report on a device that holds only alice_lb1 and alice_lb3: kept, not opened, tried again when keys arrive.

confirm.note: sealed.md §5.2 step 2b, kind 8563: "It was me" answered once for all my devices. Added by belfry-android (tools/sealed_confirm_vectors.py, which reproduces this file's other events byte for byte) on 2026-11-22; to be taken into services/onboarding/tools/sealed_vectors.py. The rumor: kind 8563, pubkey = the confirming device (not the account), tags p (the account), device (the added device), e (the id of the roster that added it), content ""; sealed like any rumor (§4) to my own head letterbox, the seal signed by that device. A device clears its notice for the added device when the seal's signer (a) is in the roster BEFORE the one named by e, (b) is in the head now, and (c) e names the roster of my chain that added that device (in it, not in the roster before). Each case gives the opened rumor and the key that signed its seal; 'chain' is my chain for every case: root [phone], 2 adds the laptop, 3 adds the tablet and alice_extra together, 4 removes the laptop (new letterbox), anchored on 4. The cases marked 'read strictly' are Android's reading of the shape, for the lead to confirm. An 8563 is never shown as a message and never part of a shared history (8564): history.added_ids never holds one (kinds 14, 7 and 5 only).

cases.name: the phone confirms the tablet
cases.note: The phone was in roster 2, the one before roster 3 that added the tablet, and is in the head (roster 4). Accepted: the notice for the tablet goes.

cases.name: the added device confirms itself
cases.note: The tablet signs the seal. It is not in the roster before the one that added it.

cases.name: a device added in the same roster
cases.note: alice_extra came in with the tablet (roster 3): two devices added together cannot confirm each other.

cases.name: the signer is no longer in the head
cases.note: The laptop was in roster 2, before the tablet came, but roster 4 removed it.

cases.name: the signer was never in the chain
cases.note: Mallory's phone, sealed to Alice's letterbox.

cases.name: a roster that did not add the device: the one before
cases.note: e names roster 2, which added the laptop, not the tablet.

cases.name: a roster that did not add the device: a later one that keeps it
cases.note: e names roster 4: the tablet is in it, and was in roster 3 already.

cases.name: the root as the roster
cases.note: e names the root: there is no roster before it, it adds nobody.

cases.name: a roster that is not in the chain
cases.note: e is an id no roster of the chain has. Not accepted (a client may keep the wrap and judge it again when its chain moves, like any sealed rumor whose chain isn't loaded; it never clears a notice meanwhile).

cases.name: the wrong device for that roster
cases.note: Roster 3 is named, but the device is the laptop, which roster 2 added.

cases.name: p names another account
cases.note: The rumor is tagged for Bob.

cases.name: the rumor's pubkey is the account, not the device
cases.note: Step 2b: pubkey = the confirming device. Read strictly: a rumor whose pubkey is not the key that signed its seal is ignored.

cases.name: two device tags
cases.note: A tag given twice makes it invalid (as for a roster, §3.3).

cases.name: two e tags
cases.note: The same for e.

cases.name: content that is not empty
cases.note: Step 2b: content "". Read strictly.

notes.note: Notes to myself (collective-belfry docs/one-shape.md "Notes to myself", ec048e3). Added by belfry-android (tools/sealed_notes_vectors.py, which writes this file's other sections back byte for byte) on 2026-11-23; to be taken into services/onboarding/tools/sealed_vectors.py. Notes is the ordinary direct conversation whose only participant is me: 'conversation' gives its participants (the conversation id is each platform's DM id of that set). 'rumors': what is and is not a note (expected.participants = the author and the p tags, sorted; notes = that set is exactly me). 'wrap': the first rumor sealed (§4) to my own head letterbox by my phone, on the chain 'a valid root' (not ready): the ONLY wrap of a note, since the recipient's copy and the self-copy are the same. 'plans': how a note is sent by 'device' given what the relay answered about my chain ('chain' null = no anchor; 'answer' complete = after authentication and to EOSE). Notes never waits for `ready`, and on a device that can seal a note is never sent the old way. No typing event (kind 21059 / 20002) is ever sent for this conversation. The row is the first of Messages, never unread.

rumors.name: a note
rumors.note: Kind 14, pubkey = my account, exactly one p tag = my account.

rumors.name: a reply to a note
rumors.note: As in any direct conversation: ["e", <root>, "", "root"] after the p tag.

rumors.name: a picture
rumors.note: Kind 15 the same way: the one p tag first, then the file tags (dm-files.json).

rumors.name: a reaction to a note
rumors.note: Kind 7: e (the note, its author), p (its author = me), k.

rumors.name: a reaction taken back
rumors.note: Kind 5: e (the reaction), k, and the one p tag.

rumors.name: a note with no p tag
rumors.note: What older apps wrote. Read as a note: the participants of a rumor are its author and its p tags, here only me. Never written this way any more.

rumor.content: A note from before the p tag

rumors.name: a message to Bob
rumors.note: One p tag, but not mine: the conversation with Bob.

rumors.name: p names me and Bob
rumors.note: Two participants: the conversation with Bob, not Notes.

rumors.name: Bob's message to me
rumors.note: One p tag = my account, but the author is Bob: the conversation with Bob. Nobody else can write into my Notes.

wrap.name: notes: a note
wrap.note: Alice's phone seals the note to her own head letterbox (alice_lb1). The chain has no `ready`; the rumor is accepted all the same, the seal's signer being in the head.

plans.name: my chain is not ready, this device is in its head
plans.note: The not-ready case: any other conversation would wait for `ready` (§6); Notes does not. One wrap, to my own head letterbox, the seal signed by this device, no signer call.

plans.name: my chain is ready
plans.note: As any sealed conversation, with one participant: still one wrap (the self-copy is the message).

plans.name: I have a chain, this device is not in its head
plans.note: A device of mine not added yet: the note waits with the usual waiting banner until the device is added. Never the old way.

plans.name: no chain, a definite answer
plans.note: A complete answer after authentication shows no anchor: the device makes the chain now (first-device path, §5.1) and holds the note, shown as sending, until the chain is anchored; then it is sealed as in the first case. Nothing unsealed goes out.

plans.name: no chain known, the answer is not complete
plans.note: Silence, a CLOSED, an answer from before authentication: no chain is made and nothing is sent, sealed or not. The note is held, shown as sending, and decided at the first complete answer.

plans.name: an account that cannot seal
plans.note: An agent, an account that holds its own key, a guest: no device key, so no chain. One NIP-17 wrap to my own account through the signer (p = me, no lb), as old direct messages. No lock, and never the "nobody else" sentence.

silent.note: Silent wraps (collective-belfry docs/sealed.md §4 "Silent wraps", belfry-sh 27e149a). Added by belfry-android (tools/sealed_silent_vectors.py, which writes this file's other sections back byte for byte) on 2026-11-23; to be taken into services/onboarding/tools/sealed_vectors.py. A wrap (kind 1059) that addresses only its own sender carries one more tag, ["silent", "1"], on the wrap only: never in the seal or the rumor. 'carries': shape only, which wraps a client makes with it ('p' says whose key the wrap's p tag is). 'tags': which tag lists are silent; only the exact two-element tag counts, anything else is read as absent and the wrap stays valid (Android reads ["silent", "1", "x"] strictly as not silent; for the lead to confirm). 'wraps': real wraps of one note of Alice's, sealed (alice_lb1, the chain 'a valid root') and old-style: a reader opens each exactly as a wrap without the tag and ignores tags it does not know.

carries.what: sealed message: the copy to myself
carries.note: Kind 14 / 15 / 7 / 5 sealed to my own head letterbox beside the wrap for the other side.

carries.what: sealed message: the wrap for the other person
carries.note: The same rumor sealed to their head letterbox. Never silent.

carries.what: old-style message: the copy to myself
carries.note: NIP-17 through the signer, p = my account.

carries.what: old-style message: the wrap for the other person
carries.note: NIP-17 through the signer, p = their account. Never silent.
The only wrap of a note (the notes section).
On an account that cannot seal: one NIP-17 wrap to my own account.
"It was me", sealed to my own head letterbox (the confirm section).

carries.what: keys for one of my devices
carries.note: The 8561 hand-over (§5.5): a NIP-59 wrap whose p is my receiving device.
An 8564 sealed to their head letterbox (§8). Never silent.
A 1301 wrapped to the belfry's mail key (§7). Never silent; its copy to myself is.

tags.name: an old-style wrap with the tag

wraps.name: silent: a sealed note
wraps.note: Opened with alice_lb1 exactly as a wrap without the tag.

wraps.name: silent: a sealed note with tags a reader does not know
wraps.note: An unknown tag and a silent tag of another value: both ignored, the wrap opens, and it is not silent.

wraps.name: silent: an old-style note
wraps.note: NIP-17: sealed by Alice's account to itself, opened with her account key. No lb.

wraps.name: silent: an old-style note with a tag a reader does not know

join.note: sealed.md §5.7 "A device that signed in adds itself", with its "Readings fixed before the first build" and "Tightened after Android's review" (belfry-sh 1440e79). Added by belfry-android (tools/sealed_join_vectors.py, which writes this file's other sections back byte for byte, and computes every 'expected' with its own port of the reference) on 2026-11-23; to be taken into services/onboarding/tools/sealed_vectors.py. A JOIN is a roster signed by a device that is not in its prev: valid only when n = prev's + 1, its devices are exactly prev's in their order plus the signer last, its lb is a letterbox the chain never had, its signer is in no earlier roster of the path, its created_at is not before its prev's, AND it lies on the anchored path (root → the anchor's head); a client also keeps one it pinned as anchored. It is never taken in the provisional tail. A normal roster signed by a device that added itself is invalid (on the path and in the tail) while no roster after its join carries ["endorse", <that device>] signed by a device that was in the roster BEFORE that join; only that tag endorses (a roster's endorse tags come last, after `ready`), and a joiner that left the head waits for nothing. After a switch, an endorsed joiner is trusted when the endorsing device is trusted on that device. Sections: 'chains' (shape of the top-level 'chains'; 'added' where given = device → the roster that added it; 'unendorsed' = the devices of the head still limited, in the head's order), 'follow' (shape of 'follow'), 'requests' (shape of 'trust': after the steps each of 'asks' is answer_without_prompt(chain, pin, device, live_chat_devices, request_created_at, added_at, last_handover_at); 'self_added' says the roster that last added the device is signed by it, which is what makes >= apply), 'older_keys' (the decision to hand a joiner the earlier letterboxes without a prompt, from plain facts: 'keys' or 'card'), 'handover' (shape of 'keys_handover', the chain given whole; 'kept_for_later' = not taken now but kept and tried again), 'confirm' (shape of 'confirm', each case with its own chain and the devices whose added-notice is unanswered on the judging device) and 'endorsement'. 'keys' holds the test keys this section adds (made from their names like every other).

chains.name: an anchored join
chains.note: Root [phone]; roster 2, signed by the phone, adds the laptop. Roster 3 is signed by the tablet itself: the head's devices in their order, then the tablet, a new letterbox (alice_lb2). The anchor names it: valid. 'added' = for each device of the head, the roster that added it: the tablet's is its own roster.

chains.name: the same roster, not anchored
chains.note: The anchor still names roster 2. The join is nothing: anyone can sign one.

chains.name: a join is never taken in the provisional tail
chains.note: After the anchored end (roster 2) come the join and a normal roster of the phone (same prev). The join's id is the lower one; it is not a candidate: the phone's roster is the head for now.

chains.name: a join that keeps the old letterbox
chains.note: The same devices, but lb is still alice_lb1. Invalid; the anchor names an invalid roster, so the anchored path is the root alone and roster 2 follows as a valid step.

chains.name: a join that goes back to an earlier letterbox
chains.note: Roster 3 removed the laptop (alice_lb2). The tablet joins with alice_lb1, a letterbox the chain had.

chains.name: a join that drops a device
chains.note: The laptop is missing.

chains.name: a join that reorders the devices
chains.note: Laptop, phone, tablet.

chains.name: a join that adds two devices
chains.note: The tablet adds alice_extra with itself.

chains.name: a join whose signer is not the last device
chains.note: Phone, tablet, laptop.

chains.name: a join whose n skips a number
chains.note: n = 4 after roster 2.

chains.name: twenty devices, then a join
chains.note: Roster 2 has 20 devices. A join would make 21: not a roster at all (§3.1). The device asks instead (§5.2).

chains.name: a join by a device the chain had and dropped
chains.note: Roster 3 removed the laptop. Its session outlived the removal and it adds itself again: invalid (its signer is in an earlier roster of the path). It asks (§5.2).

chains.name: a join dated before its prev
chains.note: The tablet's roster is dated before roster 2. Invalid: the joiner dates its own roster, never before the one it follows.

chains.name: a join dated in the same second as its prev
chains.note: Not before: valid.

chains.name: after a join, an older device removes the joiner
chains.note: The phone (in the head before the join) signs roster 4 without the tablet, a new letterbox the tablet never gets. A normal step.

chains.name: the joiner adds a device before it is endorsed
chains.note: Roster 4, signed by the tablet, adds alice_extra. Invalid while no roster after the join carries ["endorse", tablet] signed by a device of the roster before the join. The anchor names an invalid path: the root, then roster 2 as a valid step; the join is not in a tail.

chains.name: the joiner removes a device before it is endorsed
chains.note: Roster 4, signed by the tablet, drops the phone (new letterbox). Invalid.

chains.name: the joiner only restates the roster before it is endorsed
chains.note: Roster 4, signed by the tablet: same devices, same letterbox, with ready. Invalid as well: a joiner signs nothing that counts.

chains.name: the joiner endorses itself
chains.note: Roster 4, signed by the tablet, carries ["endorse", tablet]. The tablet was not in the roster before its join, and its roster counts for nothing anyway.

chains.name: the joiner's roster in the provisional tail
chains.note: The anchor names the join; the tablet's roster 4 (adds alice_extra) comes after the anchored end. Not taken there either: the head stays the join.

chains.name: the endorsement: "It was me" on the phone
chains.note: Roster 4 = the join's devices, the join's letterbox, one ["endorse", tablet] tag, signed by the phone (in roster 2, the one before the join), with its anchor. From then on the tablet is a device like the others: 'unendorsed' is empty.

chains.name: endorsed, then the joiner adds a device
chains.note: After the endorsement the tablet signs roster 5, which adds alice_extra: valid.

chains.name: the endorsement in the provisional tail
chains.note: The anchor still names the join; the phone's endorsement (4) and then the tablet's roster 5 come after the anchored end. Both are taken for now: an endorsement is a normal roster, and it counts where it stands.

chains.name: a plain roster of an older device does not endorse
chains.note: The phone's roster 4 (ready; no endorse tag) is what devices publish by themselves. The tablet is still limited: its roster 5 is invalid. Only the tag endorses, so the limits lift only when the person taps.

chains.name: an older device's removal of another device does not endorse
chains.note: The phone's roster 4 removes the laptop and says nothing of the tablet. The tablet's roster 5 is invalid.

chains.name: a roster that keeps the joiner, without the tag: still limited
chains.note: The same roster 4 (the phone removes the laptop) as the head: valid, and 'unendorsed' still names the tablet.

chains.name: the tag counts on any roster of a device that was there before the join
chains.note: The phone's roster 4 removes the laptop AND carries ["endorse", tablet]. Validity asks only for the tag and its signer: the tablet's roster 5 is valid. ("It was me" itself publishes the same devices and the same letterbox.)

chains.name: an endorse tag for a device that is not waiting
chains.note: The phone's roster 4 names alice_extra (never in the chain) and the laptop (not a joiner). The tags are ignored, the roster is valid, the tablet is still limited.

chains.name: a joiner that left the head is no longer waiting
chains.note: The phone removes the tablet (roster 4, a new letterbox). Nothing is waiting: 'unendorsed' is empty. (It can never add itself again: the chain had it.)

chains.name: two devices add themselves, one after the other
chains.note: The tablet (roster 3, alice_lb2), then alice_new (roster 4, alice_lb3). Both valid on the anchored path, both limited.

chains.name: a joiner does not endorse an earlier joiner
chains.note: After both joins alice_new signs roster 5 with ["endorse", tablet]. It was not in the roster before the tablet's join, and it is itself not endorsed: its roster is invalid, nobody is endorsed.

chains.name: a joiner that is not endorsed does not endorse a later one
chains.note: After both joins the tablet signs roster 5 with ["endorse", alice_new]. It was in the roster before alice_new's join, but it is itself not endorsed: its roster is invalid.

chains.name: several joiners, one endorsement after both
chains.note: The laptop's roster 5 carries one endorse tag per joiner (it was in the roster before each join): both are endorsed. The tablet adds alice_extra (6), alice_new removes it (7, alice_lb4): valid.

chains.name: several joiners, the endorsement names one
chains.note: The laptop's roster 5 endorses the tablet only. The tablet's roster 6 is valid; alice_new's roster 7, after the anchored end, is not taken: it is still limited.

chains.name: the tag signed by a device that joined after
chains.note: alice_new (which joined after the tablet) is endorsed by the phone (5), then signs roster 6 with ["endorse", tablet]. Its roster is valid, but it was not in the roster before the tablet's join: the tag does nothing, and the tablet's roster 7, after the anchored end, is not taken.

chains.name: an endorsed joiner endorses a later one
chains.note: The tablet joined (3) and was endorsed by the phone (4). alice_new joins (5). The tablet was in the roster before THAT join and is a device like the others: its roster 6 with ["endorse", alice_new] is valid and endorses alice_new, whose roster 7 is valid.

chains.name: an endorsement is used once: a later joiner needs its own
chains.note: The phone endorsed the tablet (4). alice_new joins (5) and signs roster 6 at once: invalid, no roster after ITS join endorses it.

chains.name: an endorsement before the join it names does nothing
chains.note: The phone's roster 3 carries ["endorse", tablet] before the tablet has joined; the tablet then joins (4) and signs roster 5 after the anchored end: not taken, the tag must come after the join.

chains.name: two joins on the same prev: the anchor names one
chains.note: The tablet and alice_new both add themselves after roster 2. The anchor names alice_new's: the tablet's is nothing.

chains.name: the loser joins again after the winner
chains.note: The tablet read the chain again and adds itself after alice_new's join, with a NEW letterbox (alice_lb4): the one of its lost join (alice_lb2) is never reused.

chains.name: a join that lost to a roster that already holds the device
chains.note: The phone added the tablet the usual way (roster 3, same letterbox) while the tablet was adding itself. The anchor names the phone's roster: the join is discarded, the tablet is in the head and asks for the keys (§5.5).

chains.name: a join, then an anchor without a head, read without a pin
chains.note: The anchor that named the join was replaced by one with no head. A reader with no pin (the server, a new correspondent, a new device) has the root alone as anchored path and then only normal steps: roster 2, never the join. A reader that pinned the join keeps it (see follow).

follow.name: the pin follows a join
follow.note: Pinned on roster 2 (anchored). The anchor now names the join: moved, the join is the head and was seen anchored. No switch ever happened: trusted stays null (every device of the head is answered).

follow.name: a pinned join, then the anchor goes back behind it
follow.note: The join was pinned as anchored. A newer anchor names roster 2 again: not followed, the join stays (no going back holds for it like any roster).

follow.name: a stored pin whose join was never seen anchored
follow.note: A pin as no client writes it (anchored_head = roster 2, yet its path goes on to the join). The anchor names roster 2: the join is not accepted, the pin is cut back to roster 2. Reading (1): never in a pinned part the client had not itself seen anchored.

follow.name: a switch away from a join seen anchored
follow.note: The anchor leaves the join for the phone's own roster 3 (another branch of the same root): a switch. Trusted = the devices of the head held before that the new head still has: the phone and the laptop.

follow.name: after a switch, a join: the joiner is not trusted
follow.note: After the switch the tablet adds itself (roster 4). The join alone gives no trust: the device keeps the Allow card for it and hands it nothing (reading (2)).

follow.name: after a switch, endorsed by a trusted device: trusted
follow.note: The switch left this device trusting the phone and the laptop (alice_new, which the new branch added, is not). alice_extra adds itself (4): not trusted. The phone, trusted here, publishes the endorsement (5): alice_extra is trusted from then on, and the tablet it then adds (6) is too.

follow.name: after a switch, endorsed by a device that is not trusted here: the card stays
follow.note: The same, but the endorsement (5) is signed by alice_new, which this device does not trust. The chain takes it (alice_new was in the roster before the join): alice_extra may sign, and adds the tablet (6). On this device neither is trusted: the Allow card stays.

follow.name: after a switch, the joiner allowed on this device
follow.note: The person taps Allow for the tablet on this device: trusted from then on.

requests.name: the joiner's request in the same second as its join
requests.note: The tablet dates its 8562 at its own join roster's second. For a device that added itself that counts (>=, reading (3)).

requests.name: the joiner's request dated before its join
requests.note: One second before its roster: not answered.

requests.name: a device added by another device, same second
requests.note: The laptop was added by the phone (roster 2). Its request in that roster's second is not newer: not answered, as before. Only a device that added itself gets >=.

requests.name: a later request after one that was refused
requests.note: The first request (dated before the join) is refused; that is remembered for that request only. The next one is judged afresh and answered.

requests.name: the joiner is not a live chat session
requests.note: Its session is not in the list: not answered (and, §5.7, a device that follows the join removes it at once).

requests.name: the joiner's request must be newer than the last hand-over to it
requests.note: As for any device: a request dated at the last hand-over is not answered again, a newer one is.

requests.name: a pinned join the anchor went back behind
requests.note: The pin keeps the join, but the anchored end is roster 2 again, which does not hold the tablet: not answered until the anchor names the join's branch.

requests.name: after a switch the joiner goes through Allow
requests.note: Not trusted by its join (reading (2)): never answered without a prompt, whatever its request. Once allowed on this device, it is.

requests.name: after a switch, allowed here: answered
requests.note: The person allowed the tablet on this device.

older_keys.name: every condition holds
older_keys.note: The session list was read for this request and holds the joiner as a live chat session; the request is not older than the session; this device is in the head it pinned, on the anchored end, trusted; the chain never had the joiner before its join; no other device was let in today. The older letterboxes go without a prompt (what the giver holds).

older_keys.name: the session list could not be read, or does not hold a live chat session for it
older_keys.note: No hand-over. (A joiner that is no live chat session is removed at once by a device that follows its join.)

older_keys.name: the request is older than the session
older_keys.note: More than 120 s before the session was opened.

older_keys.name: the request is more than 30 days old
this device is not on the anchored end of the head it pinned
older_keys.note: A head not anchored yet, or an anchor that went back.

older_keys.name: after a switch, this device is not trusted
after a switch, the joiner is not trusted
older_keys.note: Reading (2): the card, until the person allows it here.

older_keys.name: three other devices were let in within 24 hours
older_keys.note: Devices added to my head in the last 24 hours, the joiner itself not counted; a join counts from the moment THIS device first saw it, never from the roster's own date; any other roster from its created_at. A fourth gets the card.

older_keys.name: two other devices were let in within 24 hours

handover.name: the joiner hands the new secret to the phone
handover.note: One 8561 with the join's letterbox (alice_lb2), silent, to the phone's device key. The phone follows the join: the giver is a device of its chain. Taken.

handover.name: the same hand-over before the phone has the join's roster
handover.note: The phone's chain still ends at roster 2: the giver is not in it. Not taken now, and KEPT: tried again when the chain moves (it is then the case above).

handover.name: a secret that is not its lb's
handover.note: The joiner sends alice_lb2 with another key's secret, and alice_lb4 rightly: only the pair that checks out is taken (and an lb the phone already holds is never replaced).

confirm.name: an older device confirms the joiner
confirm.note: The phone was in roster 2, the one before the join, and is in the head: accepted, the notice for the tablet goes. (The phone also publishes the endorsement roster; see 'endorsement'.)

confirm.name: the joiner confirms itself
confirm.note: The tablet is not in the roster before its own join.

confirm.name: a joiner whose own notice is unanswered here confirms a device it added
confirm.note: The tablet joined (3), the phone's roster 4 endorsed it (the tag), the tablet added alice_extra (5) and says 'It was me' for it. On THIS device the notice for the tablet is still unanswered (its 8563 has not been accepted here): the tablet's word does not count yet. Kept and judged again; the notice for alice_extra stays.

confirm.name: the same once the notice for the joiner is answered here
confirm.note: This device accepted an 8563 for the tablet (or the person tapped here): now the confirmation counts.

endorsement.note: "It was me" endorses (§5.7): besides the 8563, the device that is tapped publishes roster n+1 = the head's devices in their order, the head's lb, `ready` by the usual rule, then one ["endorse", <device>] tag per joiner it confirms (after `ready`, the last tags), signed by itself, with its anchor (§3.2). Only that tag endorses. 'before' is my chain with the unanswered join as its head; 'roster' and 'anchor' are what the phone publishes; 'after' is the chain then. Remove needs no endorsement: it is a roster of an older device already.

endorsement_by_allow.note: Allow on the card endorses too (§5.7 "From Android's first build of reading"): when a joiner's older keys need the card and the person taps Allow on an older device, that device hands the keys and publishes the endorsement roster exactly as "It was me" does (same devices, same lb, one endorse tag, its anchor). Here the laptop is tapped. Android also sends the 8563 ('confirmation') so the notice goes on the other devices: the same decision, said once. Appended after the section's first publication; nothing before this key changed.
